weekly.title: Carney, at a Cabinet Retreat, Considers Further Trade Strikes Against the U.S.
weekly.summary: Canada’s retaliation this week against President Trump’s tariffs was met with more American tariffs and a closed U.S. border on some Canadian products.

weekly.title: Choking Global Trade
weekly.summary: Low rainfall and shrinking rivers are causing shipping bottlenecks, and higher prices, around the world.

weekly.title: Iran-backed terror group’s latest territorial grab threatens second global shipping chokepoint
weekly.summary: Iran-backed Houthi forces seized Yemen's Mocha port and advanced toward Bab el-Mandeb, threatening Red Sea shipping as Brent crude surged past $106.

weekly.title: Moscow Claims Ukraine Planned to Start a War Between Russia and the U.K.
weekly.summary: Britain warned that Russia uses disinformation to divide Ukraine from its international partners.

weekly.title: Steve Witkoff, Trump’s Special Envoy, Made More Than $250 Million While in Government
weekly.summary: A disclosure shows that Steve Witkoff collected nearly $107 million in 2025 from a holding company that includes a crypto business owned by his family and President Trump’s.

weekly.title: Trump’s Trade War With Canada Is Making Even Sprinkle Makers Nervous
weekly.summary: President Trump’s levies on a long, eclectic list of products from Canada have companies scrambling to figure out if their supply chains are affected.

weekly.title: Voters Are Asking A.I. About Elections. The Answers Can Vary by User.
weekly.summary: Artificial intelligence is quickly becoming a go-to stop for voters looking for information about political races. Researchers are studying the effects.

weekly.title: European Central Bank Raises Rates in Bid to Quell Inflation
weekly.summary: The bank, fighting price pressures spurred by the war in the Middle East, raised its benchmark rate to 2.5 percent.

weekly.title: Clay, an A.I. Sales Tool Provider, Raises $115 Million
weekly.summary: The round was led by Wellington Management, a firm known for investing in start-ups on the path toward potential initial public offerings.

weekly.title: Jimmy Kimmel Moves Talarico Interview to YouTube Because of F.C.C. ‘Threat’
weekly.summary: In a monologue on Wednesday, Mr. Kimmel said that the show made the decision because the F.C.C. had “threatened” ABC over “traditional editorial decisions.”

weekly.title: Why is Apple’s New Foldable iPhone Duo $1,999?
weekly.summary: The company unveiled a new iPhone that costs $1,999. Here are the economics behind that price tag.

weekly.title: A.I. Data Center Pollution Poses Health Threat, Former E.P.A. Officials Warn
weekly.summary: Air pollution from gas-fired power plants to run data centers is expected to add at least $20 billion in annual health care costs by 2028, the group warns.

weekly.title: Fire aboard cargo ship undergoing repairs at busy Chinese port leaves 25 people dead, five more injured
weekly.summary: A cargo ship called the Ocean Melody caught fire during repairs at Qingdao port, killing 25 of the 42 people on board the Liberian-flagged vessel.

weekly.title: Why Yemen Is Back on the Brink of War
weekly.summary: The Houthi militia, the Yemeni government, Iran and Saudi Arabia all have reasons to escalate the conflict. Here’s what to know.

weekly.title: Kenneth Feinberg Recalls Running the 9/11 Compensation Fund
weekly.summary: Kenneth Feinberg says the nearly three years he spent running the Sept. 11 compensation fund changed his life view forever.

weekly.title: Help! We Canceled a Vacation Rental 2 Years Ago. Where’s Our $13,000?
weekly.summary: In July 2024, a couple used Booking.com to reserve two apartments in Hawaii, but quickly changed their minds. Getting a refund was no day at the beach.

weekly.title: Cargo Ship Fire in Eastern China Kills 25
weekly.summary: The ship was docked in the port city of Qingdao for repairs at the time of the blaze, whose cause remained unclear, according to state media.

weekly.title: Eurail, the Longtime Savior of Shoestring Backpackers, Ditches Its Name
weekly.summary: The flexible train ticket is rebranding itself as the Interrail Pass. For many travelers, the old name evokes a bygone era of freewheeling European travel.

weekly.title: Saudi Oil Exports Plunge as Spread of War Shuts Off Shipping Routes
weekly.summary: With few good options for safely shipping oil, Saudi Arabia’s exports have fallen to a 13-year low.

weekly.title: Russian Drone Incursion Delayed Zelensky Flight to Oslo, Moldova Says
weekly.summary: An airspace closure delayed the Ukrainian leader’s trip between Moldova and Norway, officials said. They did not confirm a claim by Norway’s prime minister that a drone had “almost hit” the plane.

weekly.title: A $5,000 ‘Trump Dividend’? The Bond Market May Like a Word.
weekly.summary: President Trump’s latest political gambit could cost more than $1 trillion, and further roil a volatile bond market.

weekly.title: Why November Is Becoming the Best Time for Off-Season Travel
weekly.summary: The increasing popularity of September and October travel has changed the traditional shoulder season, leaving sporadic midweek troughs and a few weeks in November.

weekly.title: How 9/11 transformed synagogue security into a new reality for the Jewish community
weekly.summary: FBI data shows Jews face 63% of religiously motivated hate crimes as communities prepare for Rosh Hashanah on Friday, Sept. 11 amid rising threats.

weekly.title: With Messaging That Mirrors Putin’s, Germany’s Far-Right Party Gains Ground
weekly.summary: Embracing positions extolled by the Kremlin, the Alternative for Germany party may govern for the first time in a German state.

weekly.title: Drone nearly strikes Zelenskyy’s plane before takeoff for Norwegian king’s funeral, PM says
weekly.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's plane was reportedly almost hit by a Russian drone during takeoff from Moldova, closing Chișinău airspace.

weekly.title: Justice Dept. Investigates Nvidia Deal With Groq
weekly.summary: The Justice Department is examining whether the tech giant sought to sidestep antitrust scrutiny.

weekly.title: Anthropic Researchers Raise Alarm Over A.I. Acceleration, Warning of Threat to Humanity
weekly.summary: Their warnings echo concerns that other artificial intelligence experts have voiced in recent months, as calls increase for a slowdown in the pace of development.

weekly.title: Spanish opposition leader calls prime minister a ‘traitor’ over Ceuta migrant crisis
weekly.summary: Santiago Abascal branded Pedro Sánchez a "traitor" in parliament over Spain's migrant crisis in the North African enclave of Ceuta amid protests.

weekly.title: Apple Unveils the iPhone Duo, a Foldable Phone That Costs $1,999
weekly.summary: At the company’s annual September product event, Apple also demonstrated its work on artificial intelligence and other new devices.

weekly.title: Bond Market Rebuffs Treasury’s $6 Billion Plan to Reduce Borrowing Costs
weekly.summary: The 10-year yield rose to its highest level in three years, suggesting investors were underwhelmed by the details of a move to buy back government bonds.

weekly.title: Hunter Biden’s ‘Laptop’ Crypto Coin Plummets Upon Launching
weekly.summary: The president’s son portrayed his memecoin as a symbol of redemption. Critics denounced it as hypocrisy.

weekly.title: Trump’s Midterm Pitch Clouded by Iran War and Canada Tariffs
weekly.summary: A worsening trade war and a spike in oil prices could create new economic risks as the president prepares to rally Republicans for the midterms.

weekly.title: Ukraine strikes deep into Russia’s Arctic gas heartland as Trump pushes Putin toward peace
weekly.summary: Ukrainian drones struck Novy Urengoy, sparking a fire in Russia's top natural-gas region roughly 1,740 miles from Ukraine's border in the Arctic.

weekly.title: Israel’s E1 plan explained: The Jerusalem-area corridor sparking international backlash
weekly.summary: Israel says E1 construction in the West Bank falls under the Oslo Accords, but Britain imposed sanctions. And 11 nations weigh trade restrictions on settlements.

weekly.title: Joseph Rice, Lowcountry Lawyer Who Took On Big Tobacco, Dies at 72
weekly.summary: He challenged tobacco companies as well as the opioid industry, securing multibillion-dollar settlements that also benefited public health.

weekly.title: Why California Is Reconsidering Its Decision to Shun Nuclear Power
weekly.summary: The state is considering extending the life of its last nuclear power plant, Diablo Canyon, and allowing construction of new reactors to help meet its clean energy goals.

weekly.title: Measuring the Cost of Trump’s Multiple Wars
weekly.summary: Voters and some Republican lawmakers are growing weary of President Trump’s trade battles and the economic fallout from fighting in the Middle East.

weekly.title: A.I. Music Giant Suno Tries to Play Nice With Record Labels
weekly.summary: Suno has drawn copyright lawsuits from the majors. Now it is releasing a version of its A.I. music generator trained in partnership with Warner Music.

weekly.title: US sinks another 'floating refueling station' linked to 'narco-terrorist' group
weekly.summary: The United States military on Sept. 8 sank another vessel that it described as a "floating refueling station" involved with the Los Choneros.

weekly.title: 70 Americans still unaccounted for after catastrophic Nepal flooding
weekly.summary: Officials say 70 Americans remain unaccounted for after catastrophic flooding along the Nepal-China border, while warning the region remains too dangerous for travelers.

weekly.title: Meta Introduces Muse, an A.I. Agent That Can Send Your Emails and Book Your Travel
weekly.summary: Muse, Meta’s new A.I. agent, acts as a personal digital assistant that connects to Facebook and Instagram, as well as third-party apps such as Spotify and OpenTable.

weekly.title: Philippines defense chief calls out China after note interrupts remarks at Seoul forum: 'Coercion, bullying'
weekly.summary: Gilberto Teodoro read aloud a note from China handed to him mid-speech at the Seoul Defense Dialogue, calling it actual coercion and bullying.

weekly.title: NATO member boots 10 Russian diplomats
weekly.summary: Hungary demands that 10 members of the Russian mission leave the country, alleging that they engaged in actions that were "unacceptable," according to the Vienna Convention.

weekly.title: A Hacking Tool Built With A.I. Can Breach Phones Without a Click
weekly.summary: An attack discovered by A.I. researchers could have compromised hundreds of millions of devices within hours, experts said.

weekly.title: Apple Expected to Unveil a Folding iPhone at Annual Launch Event
weekly.summary: Fans of the company’s products widely believe it will unveil a folding smartphone at its annual launch event on Wednesday.

weekly.title: Video captures grocery store manager's daring rescue of toddler who ran into oncoming traffic
weekly.summary: Security footage captures Luis Cruz diving into a busy Puebla, Mexico, road to rescue a 3-year-old girl moments before a minivan crosses her path.

weekly.title: Britain’s dramatic crackdown on Israeli settlements sparks fierce response as US blowback looms
weekly.summary: Ed Miliband announced U.K. sanctions targeting Israeli West Bank settlements, prompting U.S. Ambassador Mike Huckabee to warn of economic consequences.

weekly.title: Art heist thieves make off with Renoir paintings worth millions from museum on French Riviera
weekly.summary: Two thieves cut through a fence at the French Riviera's Renoir Museum in Cagnes-sur-Mer, stealing four paintings but dropping two as police closed in.

weekly.title: Is the Iran-backed terrorist movement Hezbollah on the ropes in Lebanon?
weekly.summary: Israel's capture of the Ali al-Taher ridge dealt a severe blow to Iran's Axis of Resistance, but experts warn Hezbollah is still rebuilding.

weekly.title: Key App Developers Have Yet to Embrace Apple’s New Siri A.I.
weekly.summary: For the company’s new artificial intelligence system to take off, it will need plenty of support from the makers of popular apps on Apple’s phones.

weekly.title: Russian strikes continue following visit by Witkoff and Kushner to Kyiv
weekly.summary: Russia launched ballistic and cruise missiles at Kyiv shortly after envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner's visit to the city for peace negotiations.

weekly.title: Virtual Taekwondo Takes the Contact Out of a Combat Sport
weekly.summary: The contactless version of the Korean martial art is making its debut at this year’s Asian Games. Critics say it’s a glorified video game.

weekly.title: UK moves to sanction Israeli settlements as PM Burnham risks clash with Trump: report
weekly.summary: Andy Burnham's UK sanctions targeting Israeli West Bank settlements spark fierce backlash from Benjamin Netanyahu's ministers and U.S. lawmakers.

weekly.title: Popular TV host, media star faces hanging after conviction in major synthetic drug trafficking case
weekly.summary: Sarah Khalifa was among 12 defendants sentenced to death after prosecutors accused the group of manufacturing and trafficking synthetic narcotics.

weekly.title: Russia’s quieter nuclear submarines threaten NATO, former commander warns
weekly.summary: Russia's Yasen-M submarines and militarized Kola Peninsula are forcing NATO to confront a growing undersea threat across the GIUK Gap and Arctic, expert warns.

weekly.title: Early Data Indicates an A.I.-Generated Drug Could Slow Aging
weekly.summary: Artificial intelligence was used to help develop a drug candidate, rentosertib, for a rare lung condition. Its maker says the drug also seems to reduce the biological hallmarks of age.

developing.title: Live Updates: Germany’s Far Right Tops Key State Race, but Falls Short of Power
developing.summary: The Alternative for Germany party is projected to finish first in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt. But lacking a majority, without the help of other parties it cannot become the first far-right party to govern a state since 1945.
